content: The Founder stands over the brown paper with his hands in his pockets. 'Three to four weeks is what I told Archive 001 buyers. The report even has a gift buyer getting it early. Why isn't that enough?'
round_time: Morning, Day 2 - Pain point 9: 3-4 week wait with no delivery date

content: Head of Product carries the marker over to the packing bench and pins PP9 above Ops' timeline, moving the meeting to where the constraint physically lives.
round_time: Morning, Day 2 - Pain point 9: 3-4 week wait with no delivery date

content: Research answers before Ops can. 'Because a gift buyer doesn't plan around three to four weeks. They plan around a birthday. The report's gift buyers worried about delivery more than anyone, but that's simulated. The real question is how many real buyers bought for a date. One checkout question would tell us: is this a gift, and is there a date it needs to arrive by?'
round_time: Morning, Day 2 - Pain point 9: 3-4 week wait with no delivery date

proposals.text: Add one optional checkout/waitlist question: 'Is this a gift? Is there a date it must arrive by?'
proposals.test: share of real buyers with a deadline

content: Brand watches the reel loop for the fourth time and says nothing. They notice the frame where Growth wants to drop in a 'ships in 21 days' sticker and wince.
round_time: Morning, Day 2 - Pain point 9: 3-4 week wait with no delivery date

content: The Designer leans over the timeline. 'Add the lid card to your critical path. Printing has its own lead time, and it has to be inside the tin before you seal it.'
round_time: Morning, Day 2 - Pain point 9: 3-4 week wait with no delivery date

content: The Plant Specialist looks at the dates on the brown paper and thinks about the season. A marigold sown when Archive 002 arrives won't behave the same as one sown in Archive 001's window. They decide to raise it when the timeline comes up. Not yet.
round_time: Morning, Day 2 - Pain point 9: 3-4 week wait with no delivery date

content: Growth taps the phone screen. 'Give me one number. Ships in 21 days. A date in the hook converts. Three to four weeks reads like we don't know, and the report's people heard exactly that.'
round_time: Morning, Day 2 - Pain point 9: 3-4 week wait with no delivery date

proposals.text: Put a specific dispatch promise ('ships in 21 days') in the reel hook
proposals.test: reel conversion with vs without a date

disagreement: Growth (specific date in the hook now) vs Ops (no date until painting is timed)

content: Community winces. 'And if we miss 21 days, the reel ends up as a screenshot in someone's story. A missed date is worse than no date.'
round_time: Morning, Day 2 - Pain point 9: 3-4 week wait with no delivery date

content: CX offers a middle path. 'Even without a date, I can stop the silence. Proposal: a weekly order update to every buyer. Painting started, half done, packed, shipped. A photo from the bench each time. The wait feels shorter when you can see it moving.'
round_time: Morning, Day 2 - Pain point 9: 3-4 week wait with no delivery date

proposals.text: Weekly order update to every buyer through the wait (painting started / half done / packed / shipped) with a bench photo
proposals.test: 'where is my order' DM count vs Archive 001

content: Ops plants a palm flat on the timeline. 'No. I'm not giving you 21 days. I don't know how long one tin takes, never mind 100, never mind a batch with a printed card and a new seed process. A simulated parcel arriving early tells me nothing about real painting time. Give me a timed run of ten tins this week and I'll give you a date with a margin built in. Until then, the honest wording is the range we already use.'
round_time: Morning, Day 2 - Pain point 9: 3-4 week wait with no delivery date

proposals.text: Timed painting pilot: paint 10 tins end to end, measure time per tin, then set a dispatch date with a buffer
proposals.test: actual vs promised dispatch on Archive 002

content: Finance connects it to yesterday: every day of buffer Ops adds protects the refund cap. Growth's 21 days, if missed, triggers exactly the refunds they fought about. They side with Ops, but don't say so yet.
round_time: Morning, Day 2 - Pain point 9: 3-4 week wait with no delivery date

content: Legal unmutes. 'A specific dispatch claim in an ad has to be true when you make it and true when it ships. If it isn't, the remedy promise kicks in and the claim itself could be a problem. Proposal: no specific date in creative until Ops signs it off. Verify with a professional.'
round_time: Morning, Day 2 - Pain point 9: 3-4 week wait with no delivery date
